postures.note: FAKE example entry. The strictest posture: the project is not named, described, or acknowledged in public writing.
postures.say: Nothing. The project is not named, described, or acknowledged in public writing.
postures.shelf: Private shelf only; nothing about the project lives in the repository.

postures.note: FAKE example entry. The open posture: the project may be named and the work on it described in general terms, while findings and case material still move only through the formal channels.
postures.say: The project may be named in public writing, and the work on it described in general terms.
postures.shelf: Public shelf for the name and the general description; findings and case material stay on the private shelf until disclosed through the formal channel.

postures.note: FAKE example entry. The hybrid posture: the project may be named in public writing, and nothing about the work on it is said.
postures.say: The project may be named in public writing. Nothing about the work on it is said.
postures.shelf: Public shelf for the name alone; everything else on the private shelf.

postures.note: FAKE example entry. A retired posture, kept so old tagging files still resolve: the checker flags any project still assigned it and names its successor. Its tag is never reused.
postures.say: The project may be named in public writing, and progress on the work reported in general terms.
postures.shelf: Public shelf for the name and general progress; everything else on the private shelf.
